rationale: Multiple possible discovery paths and vague outputs make scope too broad for a reliable estimate.

evidence: view thumbnail sequences of video segments
rationale: Thumbnail sequence viewing is a concrete UI feature with clear scope.

evidence: get info about similar video items and segments
rationale: Similarity and the type of information are too vague to form a reasonable implementation estimate.

evidence: perceptually similar video items and segments
rationale: Perceptual similarity is technically broad and underspecified, making estimation difficult.

evidence: content recommendations from similar profiles
rationale: Similar profiles and recommendation behavior are not specified enough for reliable estimation.

evidence: most relevant news events in my area
rationale: Relevance and area are vague, leaving scope too broad to estimate.

evidence: identify persons in videos, and receive related information about them
rationale: Person identification plus related information retrieval is broad and underspecified.

evidence: identify products in videos, and receive related information about them
rationale: Product identification scope is very large and the related information is unspecified.

evidence: identify broadcaster logos in videos, and receive related information about them
rationale: Broadcaster logos are a bounded class and the information lookup can be estimated reasonably.

evidence: identify brands in videos
rationale: Brands are an unbounded and broad set, making scope difficult to estimate.

evidence: recommended with videos related to that picture or image
rationale: Video recommendation based on image similarity is broad and underspecified.

evidence: see, validate and edit segmentation of videos
rationale: This is a concrete admin tool for video segmentation review and editing.

evidence: annotate news video segments and extract a topic for each segment
rationale: Segment annotation and topic extraction are defined enough for a reasonable implementation estimate.

evidence: filter and rank videos based on A/V quality aspects
rationale: A/V quality aspects are vague and numerous, making scope too broad to estimate.

evidence: quick assessment of whether audio material has been edited before the upload
rationale: Audio editing detection is a specific enough objective.

evidence: prefilter nudity content
rationale: Nudity prefiltering is a clear, bounded classification task.

evidence: search based on low-level asset information
rationale: Low-level asset information is vague, leaving the search scope underdefined.

evidence: automatically validated the ingested contents for copyright infringement
rationale: Copyright infringement validation is a very broad legal-technical capability.

evidence: prefilter the content using search on high-level asset information such as metadata and tags

evidence: assess how interesting or appealing or complex a picture is

rationale: Numeric limit is explicit and unambiguous.

rationale: Join mechanism (open URL, enter name) is clear.

rationale: The object to display (current item being estimated) is clear in this domain context.

evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
rationale: Scope and object are clear; no materially different interpretations.

rationale: “Immediately” is vague about timing/trigger (real-time push vs polling vs refresh), leading to different functional expectations.

evidence: shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
rationale: Reveal condition (after all have estimated) and simultaneous display are clearly stated.

evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
rationale: Defines a clear cutoff event for when changes are allowed.

evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
rationale: “Prior estimates” is ambiguous (prior rounds in same game vs across games; only this session vs historical), changing what data must be shown.

evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
rationale: Scope (“current round”) and mapping (estimator to estimate) are clear.

evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
rationale: Ambiguous about who can start it (any participant vs specific roles), and what “start” entails if already running, leading to different behaviors.

evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
rationale: “As soon as” is vague and “we all play an estimate” could mean when last card is selected vs when estimates are revealed, yielding different reset timing.

evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
rationale: “Scroll back through” is vague about UI/extent (within current game only vs across games; how far back; what is included), allowing different interpretations.

evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
rationale: “Same order” is underspecified (what the canonical order is; whether configurable; how special cards are ordered), leading to different implementations.

rationale: “Draw has not been completed” is ambiguous (completed when all have selected vs when revealed vs when moderator accepts), affecting when changes are allowed.

rationale: “Compliant” and “standards” are ambiguous without specifying versions/levels and what constitutes compliance, allowing materially different interpretations.

rationale: “Commonly used terms” is vague (which terms, where used, completeness criteria), leading to different scopes for the list.

rationale: “As fast as possible” is vague and “the queries” is underspecified (which queries), enabling materially different interpretations of what indexing is required.

rationale: “Function correctly” is ambiguous (which features, acceptable degradation, layout vs functionality), allowing different interpretations of compatibility requirements.

rationale: “Where possible” is vague and “W3C accessibility guidelines” is broad without specifying version/level (e.g., WCAG 2.0 AA), leading to multiple interpretations.

evidence: respond quickly to my actions
rationale: “Quickly” is subjective and can map to different performance thresholds, yielding materially different requirements.

evidence: be able to use Unicode
rationale: “Use Unicode” is underspecified (where: names, items, exports; which normalization/encoding; storage vs display), allowing different interpretations.

evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
rationale: “Sensible and predictable” is subjective and can be interpreted in multiple materially different URL schemes.

evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
rationale: “Nice” and “something goes wrong” are vague (which errors, what content/design), enabling multiple interpretations.

evidence: stored in a non-identifiable way
rationale: “Non-identifiable” is ambiguous (anonymization vs pseudonymization; what identifiers are removed; re-identification risk threshold), leading to materially different data-handling requirements.

evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
rationale: “Some metrics” is vague (which metrics, time window, aggregation), allowing materially different interpretations of what must be provided.

rationale: Copy/paste format and parsing rules are unclear (what delimiters/columns, how multiple stories are separated), enabling materially different implementations.

evidence: browse through previous games
rationale: Browsing previous games is a clear capability; details of UI are not required to avoid multiple material interpretations.

evidence: view a transcript of a game
rationale: ‘Transcript’ is ambiguous (what exactly is included: chat/discussion, timestamps, participants, per-round events), leading to materially different outputs.

evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file

evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
rationale: ‘Transcript’ content and CSV schema (columns/rows, encoding, separators) are unspecified, allowing materially different interpretations.

evidence: change my account details
rationale: ‘Account details’ is vague (which fields: name, email, username, password, etc.), enabling materially different scopes.

evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone

rationale: The reveal condition (after all have estimated) and behavior (show all at the same time) are explicit.

evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round

evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see

evidence: reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate

evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds

evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws

evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed

evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played

evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards

evidence: a list of definitions for commonly used terms

evidence: created database indexes

evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible

evidence: respond quickly to my actions
rationale: ‘Quickly’ is vague and can be interpreted with materially different performance thresholds.

evidence: be able to use Unicode
rationale: ‘Use Unicode’ is underspecified (input only vs storage vs display; which components), enabling materially different interpretations.

evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
rationale: ‘Sensible’ and ‘predictable’ are subjective and allow materially different URL design interpretations.

evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
rationale: ‘Nice’ and ‘something goes wrong’ are vague, leading to materially different interpretations of scope and quality of error handling.

evidence: stored in a non-identifiable way
rationale: ‘Non-identifiable’ is ambiguous without specifying anonymization/pseudonymization requirements and what identifiers must be removed, leading to materially different implementations.

evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
